subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the AQA spec.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE AQA Computer Science simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: AQA defines cyber security as the processes, practices and technologies designed to do what?
options: Protect networks, computers, programs and data from attack, damage or unauthorised access
questions.explain: Cyber security protects networks, computers, programs and data from attack, damage or unauthorised access - it is about protection, not performance.

questions.q: Which of the following is a recognised AQA cyber security threat?
questions.explain: AQA lists threats including social engineering, malware, pharming, weak/default passwords, misconfigured access rights, removable media and unpatched/outdated software.

questions.q: What best describes social engineering?
options: Encrypting data with a strong key
Backing up files to the cloud
The art of manipulating people so they give up confidential information
questions.explain: Social engineering manipulates people (rather than technology) into revealing confidential information or performing insecure actions.

questions.q: A criminal sends a fake email pretending to be a bank, asking a user to click a link and enter their login details. Which form of social engineering is this?
questions.explain: Phishing fraudulently obtains private information, often by email or SMS pretending to be a trusted organisation. Shouldering is watching over someone's shoulder; blagging uses an invented scenario.

questions.q: Watching someone enter their PIN at a cash machine to steal it is an example of which technique?
questions.explain: Shouldering (shoulder surfing) is observing a person's private information over their shoulder, such as a cashpoint PIN.

questions.q: Blagging (pretexting) involves...
options: Adding more cores to a CPU
Creating and using an invented scenario to trick a victim into divulging information
questions.explain: Blagging creates a believable but invented scenario to increase the chance the victim gives up information or performs actions they normally would not.

questions.q: What is malware?
options: A type of high-level programming language
An umbrella term for hostile or intrusive software
questions.explain: Malware is an umbrella term covering many forms of hostile or intrusive software, including viruses, trojans and spyware.

questions.q: Software that secretly records what a user types and sends it to an attacker is best described as which form of malware?
questions.explain: Spyware secretly gathers information about a user, such as keystrokes, and passes it to a third party. AQA lists viruses, trojans and spyware as forms of malware.

questions.q: Which best describes a trojan?
options: A gate used in Boolean logic
Malware disguised as, or hidden inside, a legitimate-looking program that the user runs
A device that stores data magnetically
questions.explain: A trojan is malware disguised as a harmless or useful program; when the user runs it, it carries out its malicious payload.

questions.q: What is pharming?
options: A way of speeding up internet downloads
A cyber attack that redirects a website's traffic to a fake website
A method of backing up a database
questions.explain: Pharming is a cyber attack intended to redirect a website's traffic to a fake (bogus) website in order to steal information.

questions.q: Why are weak or default passwords a security threat?
options: They are easy for attackers to guess or look up, giving unauthorised access
questions.explain: Weak or unchanged default passwords are easy to guess or find, letting attackers gain unauthorised access to systems and accounts.

questions.q: What does the threat of 'misconfigured access rights' mean?
options: A monitor set to the wrong resolution
A cable plugged into the wrong port
Users being given permissions they should not have, so they can reach data they should not
questions.explain: Misconfigured access rights mean permissions are set incorrectly, so users can access files or systems they should not be able to, creating a security risk.

questions.q: What is the purpose of penetration testing?
options: To physically clean the inside of a computer
To attempt to gain access to resources to find security weaknesses before real attackers do
questions.explain: Penetration testing deliberately attempts to gain access to resources without normal credentials, to find and fix vulnerabilities before genuine attackers exploit them.

questions.q: AQA identifies two types of penetration testing. One simulates an attack from a malicious insider. What does the other simulate?
options: An attack from outside the system with no knowledge of credentials
questions.explain: One type simulates an insider who has some knowledge/credentials; the other simulates an external attacker with no knowledge of any credentials for the target system.

questions.q: Which of these is a method AQA lists to detect or prevent cyber security threats?
questions.explain: AQA lists automatic software updates, along with biometrics, password systems, CAPTCHA and email confirmations, as measures to detect and prevent threats.

questions.q: A website sends a message to your email address with a link you must click to activate your account. What is this an example of?
options: Using email confirmation to confirm a user's identity
questions.explain: Sending an email confirmation that the user must act on helps confirm the person's identity and that they control that email account.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a CAPTCHA?
options: To help distinguish a human user from an automated bot
questions.explain: A CAPTCHA presents a challenge that is easy for humans but hard for automated programs, helping to block bots from misusing a system.

questions.q: Which of these is a biometric security measure, particularly useful on mobile devices?
questions.explain: Biometric measures use physical characteristics such as fingerprints or facial recognition to authenticate a user, and are common on mobile devices.

questions.q: What does the Computer Misuse Act 1990 make illegal?
options: Gaining unauthorised access to computer material, e.g. hacking
Buying a computer without a receipt
questions.explain: The Computer Misuse Act 1990 makes unauthorised access to computer systems (hacking), and unauthorised access with intent to commit further offences or to modify data, illegal.

questions.q: What is the main aim of data protection legislation such as the Data Protection Act 2018?
options: To make all data free for anyone to read
To ban the use of databases
To control how organisations collect, store and use people's personal data
questions.explain: Data protection law controls how organisations handle personal data, requiring it to be used fairly, kept secure and used only for stated purposes.
